ann_87.original: Heavy-use detector for customers without a voice-mail plan. It stays off for most customers and switches on when daytime minutes are high, with evening minutes, night minutes and day charge adding to it; a voice-mail plan raises its threshold so far that it acts on 6 of the 1061 voice-mail customers in training, against 1217 of the 2939 customers without one. The Louisiana indicator also pushes it down: it acts on 0 of the 65 Louisiana customers in training. It acts on 1223 training customers, whose observed churn rate is 24.7% against 9.5% for the other 2777; for those it acts on, switching it off lowers the score by 2.21 logits on average (this counts what it passes to the heavy-use hinge and what it holds back in the service-call gate). Switching it off drops the training AUC from 0.926 to 0.675. Self-probe (whole model, typical customer, no voice-mail plan, day charge matched to minutes): predicted risk is 0.8% at 200 day minutes, 4.1% at 250 and 99.3% at 300, with this part's exit at 1.78 at 300; the same 300-minute customer with a voice-mail plan stays at 0.4%, the exit at 0.00.
ann_87.proposed: This part scores daytime, evening and night-time use: more daytime minutes raise the predicted chance that a customer leaves in an uneven way, even more so with evening minutes above 201 minutes, and the other way for customers with a voice-mail plan.

ann_88.original: Complaint signal for customers who are not heavy daytime users. Customer-service calls open this gate and each further call raises it, but the usage score enters it with a large negative weight, so as daytime use rises the gate closes and calls count for less; for customers on the heavy-use hinge it acts on 0 of 372. Self-probe (whole model, typical customer): the gate is 0.00 at 2 calls and 0.33 at 3, and predicted risk is 0.9% at 2 calls, 2.7% at 3, 13.7% at 4 and 83.8% at 6. For a heavy daytime user (300 minutes, day charge 51 dollars) the gate stays at 0.00 even at 6 calls, and predicted risk is 99.3% at 0 calls and 99.3% at 6. In training the gate acts on 616 customers, whose observed churn rate is 25.2% against 12.1% for the rest, adding 2.24 logits on average for them. Of the 318 customers with 4 or more calls (observed churn 50.0%) it acts on 255; among the 88 of them whose usage score is on, it acts on 25. Switching it off drops the training AUC from 0.926 to 0.842.
ann_88.proposed: This part turns calls to customer service into a higher predicted chance that a customer leaves from about 3 calls upwards, rising slowly at first, then faster.

In training it acts on 372 customers, whose observed churn rate is 66.7% against 8.8% for the rest, adding 3.61 logits on average for them; the service-call gate acts on 0 of these customers. Switching it off drops the training AUC from 0.926 to 0.903.

ann_96.original: How heavy use and complaints share out the risk. The usage score adds risk itself and through the heavy-use hinge, and at the same time holds the service-call gate shut, so a customer is flagged either as a heavy daytime user or as a frequent caller, and calls stop counting once daytime use is high enough to switch on the heavy-use hinge. The voice-mail plan splits heavy daytime users: of customers with 250 or more day minutes, the 305 without a voice-mail plan have observed churn 60.7% and mean predicted risk 61.5%, the 88 with one have observed churn 8.0% and mean predicted risk 7.1%. ann_97.original: The predicted churn probability is the sigmoid of a bias plus the parts' contributions, added on the logit scale. Three routes carry most of the risk: heavy daytime use without a voice-mail plan (usage_service), frequent service calls among other customers (also usage_service) and the international plan (intl_plan_gate); the day-charge counterweight, tenure, state offsets, small usage hinges and direct terms shift the score by smaller amounts. The root has no direct input edges of its own: 0 found. The day-call count, night-call count, night charge, area code 415 and the indicators of most states feed nothing and are unconnected entries of the root. Self-probe (whole model, typical customer): because the parts add on the logit scale, the routes compound: predicted risk is 0.9% with 1 call and no international plan, 13.7% with 4 calls, 15.0% with the plan and 76.4% with both; the plan adds 3.02 logits at 1 call and 3.02 at 4. The annotated model reproduces the network to within 3.3e-16 on the training rows.

An international plan and heavy daytime use raise the predicted chance that a customer leaves by large amounts, heavy daytime use in an uneven way; calls to customer service raise it from about 3 calls upwards; state, account length and the other usage figures shift it by small amounts.

parts.original_hypothesis: The predicted churn probability is the sigmoid of a bias plus the parts' contributions, added on the logit scale. Three routes carry most of the risk: heavy daytime use without a voice-mail plan (usage_service), frequent service calls among other customers (also usage_service) and the international plan (intl_plan_gate); the day-charge counterweight, tenure, state offsets, small usage hinges and direct terms shift the score by smaller amounts. The root has no direct input edges of its own: 0 found. The day-call count, night-call count, night charge, area code 415 and the indicators of most states feed nothing and are unconnected entries of the root. Self-probe (whole model, typical customer): because the parts add on the logit scale, the routes compound: predicted risk is 0.9% with 1 call and no international plan, 13.7% with 4 calls, 15.0% with the plan and 76.4% with both; the plan adds 3.02 logits at 1 call and 3.02 at 4. The annotated model reproduces the network to within 3.3e-16 on the training rows.
variables: number of calls to customer service

parts.name: usage_service
parts.original_hypothesis: How heavy use and complaints share out the risk. The usage score adds risk itself and through the heavy-use hinge, and at the same time holds the service-call gate shut, so a customer is flagged either as a heavy daytime user or as a frequent caller, and calls stop counting once daytime use is high enough to switch on the heavy-use hinge. Self-probe (whole model): for a heavy daytime user (300 minutes) predicted risk is 99.3% at 0 calls and 99.3% at 6, while for the typical customer it is 0.9% and 83.8%. In training the service-call gate acts on 0 of the 372 customers on the heavy-use hinge. The voice-mail plan splits heavy daytime users: of customers with 250 or more day minutes, the 305 without a voice-mail plan have observed churn 60.7% and mean predicted risk 61.5%, the 88 with one have observed churn 8.0% and mean predicted risk 7.1%. Switching the whole composition off drops the training AUC from 0.926 to 0.594.
variables: number of calls to customer service

parts.name: usage_score
parts.original_hypothesis: Heavy-use detector for customers without a voice-mail plan. It stays off for most customers and switches on when daytime minutes are high, with evening minutes, night minutes and day charge adding to it; a voice-mail plan raises its threshold so far that it acts on 6 of the 1061 voice-mail customers in training, against 1217 of the 2939 customers without one. The Louisiana indicator also pushes it down: it acts on 0 of the 65 Louisiana customers in training. It acts on 1223 training customers, whose observed churn rate is 24.7% against 9.5% for the other 2777; for those it acts on, switching it off lowers the score by 2.21 logits on average (this counts what it passes to the heavy-use hinge and what it holds back in the service-call gate). Switching it off drops the training AUC from 0.926 to 0.675. Self-probe (whole model, typical customer, no voice-mail plan, day charge matched to minutes): predicted risk is 0.8% at 200 day minutes, 4.1% at 250 and 99.3% at 300, with this part's exit at 1.78 at 300; the same 300-minute customer with a voice-mail plan stays at 0.4%, the exit at 0.00.

parts.name: heavy_usage_hinge
parts.original_hypothesis: A second, steeper slope for the heaviest daytime users. It reads the usage score and switches on once that score passes a threshold, so above that point extra day minutes raise the risk faster. In training it acts on 372 customers, whose observed churn rate is 66.7% against 8.8% for the rest, adding 3.61 logits on average for them; the service-call gate acts on 0 of these customers. Switching it off drops the training AUC from 0.926 to 0.903.

Self-probe (whole model, typical customer, international minutes and charge held): predicted risk falls from 1.22% at 1 international call to 0.43% at 10. parts.name: minutes_hinges
parts.original_hypothesis: Four small usage hinges. International minutes above about the typical level raise the score (heavy international callers look riskier); night minutes and evening charge lower it; a hinge on night minutes plus the Indiana and Tennessee indicators raises it. Self-probe (whole model, typical customer): this part contributes -0.13 logits at 10 international minutes and 0.21 at 20; -0.04 at 150 night minutes and -0.21 at 350; -0.13 at an evening charge of 17 dollars and -0.24 at 30. The international-minutes hinge is on for 1209 training customers (observed churn 16.8% against 13.0%). Together the four barely matter: switching the part off moves the training AUC from 0.9261 to 0.9258. The night-minutes, evening-charge and Indiana/Tennessee hinges are described, not explained: they are small corrections with no clear domain reading.

reference_patient.definition: the typical patient: the median training patient for every number and the most common training category for every category (not a real patient); an input the data ties to a category takes its typical value within that category (linked inputs)

confidence_rules.clearly: a meaningful change in predicted risk for a typical patient (at least 5% points), the test split agrees (same sign, and its bootstrap interval over test patients excludes no benefit), and every group has at least 20 training patients
confidence_rules.consistently across patients: the claim holds for at least 90% of training patients (range across patients); this is not a significance statement
confidence_rules.on the training data only: the test split disagrees (opposite sign, or no benefit on test patients) or is unclear (its interval includes no benefit), or no test check is available
confidence_rules.slightly: the change in predicted risk for a typical patient is below 5% points
confidence_rules.the model has little data on this: a compared group has fewer than 20 training patients

settings.effect_scale: log-odds (output pre-activation) for verification; predicted risk for the typical patient for wording

ann_87.text: A higher total daytime minutes clearly raises the predicted chance that a customer leaves, and even more so if total evening minutes is above 201 minutes (in an uneven way for patients with total evening minutes above 201 minutes): for a typical customer, total daytime minutes going from 112 minutes to 249 minutes moves the predicted chance that a customer leaves from about 1% to about 14% if total evening minutes is above 201 minutes (with total evening charge at 19.88 US dollars, as in the data), and from about 2% to about 2% if total evening minutes is at or below 201 minutes (with total evening charge at 14.18 US dollars, as in the data).

Through this part, total daytime minutes clearly adds to the predicted chance that a customer leaves once it rises above about 206 minutes (between 149 and 312 minutes for different customers) (for 1617 of the 4000 training customers it already changes below that): for a typical such customer, going from 0 minutes to 271 minutes moves it from about 1% to about 79%; across patients the change happens in an uneven way.

Through this part, total daytime charge adds to the predicted chance that a customer leaves once it rises above about 35.26 US dollars (between 25.70 and 41.83 US dollars for different customers) (for 1523 of the 4000 training customers it already changes below that): for a typical such customer, going from 0.00 US dollars to 46.09 US dollars moves it from about 1% to about 77%; across patients the change happens in an uneven way (on the training data only).

Smaller effects, each changing the predicted value only slightly: a higher total daytime minutes raises it in an uneven way; a higher total daytime charge raises it in an uneven way; Louisiana (rather than any other state) lowers it; a voice-mail plan (rather than no voice-mail plan) lowers it; total daytime minutes depending on voice-mail plan raises it in an uneven way; a higher total evening minutes raises it in an uneven way; a higher total night-time minutes raises it in an uneven way; South Dakota (rather than any other state) lowers it (on the training data only).
